L0: # Pagination
L1: 
L2: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L3: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L4: 
L5: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L6: 
L7: **Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.
L8: > Nested parameters, fields, and event types on API reference pages are collapsed by default. Use the provided `?query=<name>` links to show the full definitions. Request the page with an empty `?query=` to expand every entry at once.
L9: All top-level API resources have support for bulk fetches through “list” API methods. For example, you can [list charges](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/list.md), [list customers](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/list.md), and [list invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/list.md). These list API methods share a common structure and accept, at a minimum, the following three parameters: `limit`, `starting_after`, and `ending_before`.
L10: Stripe’s list API methods use cursor-based [pagination](https://docs.stripe.com/pagination.md) through the `starting_after` and `ending_before` parameters. Both parameters accept an existing object ID value (see below) and return objects in reverse chronological order. The `ending_before` parameter returns objects listed before the named object. The `starting_after` parameter returns objects listed after the named object. These parameters are mutually exclusive.
L11: You can use either the `starting_after` or `ending_before` parameter, but not both simultaneously.
L12: Our client libraries offer [auto-pagination helpers](https://docs.stripe.com/pagination.md#auto-pagination) to traverse all pages of a list.
L13: ## Prerequisites
L14: 
L15: Before you can run the following code snippet, you need to call these APIs with the provided parameters to set up the prerequisite API object(s).
L16: 
L17: 1. createCustomer
L18: POST /v1/customers {"name":"Jenny Rosen","email":"jennyrosen@example.com"}
L19: 
L20: ## Request
L21: 
L22: ```curl
L23: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers \
L24:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>" \
L25:   -d limit=3 \
L26:   -d starting_after={{CUSTOMER_ID}}
L27: ```
L28: ### Response
L29: ```json
L30: {
L31:   "object": "list",
L32:   "url": "/v1/customers",
L33:   "has_more": false,
L34:   "data": [
L35:     {
L36:       "id": "cus_4QFJOjw2pOmAGJ",
L37:       "object": "customer",
L38:       "address": null,
L39:       "balance": 0,
L40:       "created": 1405641735,
L41:       "currency": "usd",
L42:       "default_source": "card_14HOpG2eZvKYlo2Cz4u5AJG5",
L43:       "delinquent": false,
L44:       "description": "New customer",
L45:       "discount": null,
L46:       "email": null,
L47:       "invoice_prefix": "7D11B54",
L48:       "invoice_settings": {
L49:         "custom_fields": null,
L50:         "default_payment_method": null,
L51:         "footer": null,
L52:         "rendering_options": null
L53:       },
L54:       "livemode": false,
L55:       "metadata": {
L56:         "order_id": "6735"
L57:       },
L58:       "name": "cus_4QFJOjw2pOmAGJ",
L59:       "next_invoice_sequence": 25,
L60:       "phone": null,
L61:       "preferred_locales": [],
L62:       "shipping": null,
L63:       "tax_exempt": "none",
L64:       "test_clock": null
L65:     },
L66:   ]
L67: }
L68: ```
L69: ## Parameters
L70: 
L71: - `limit` (optional, default is 10)
L72:   This specifies a limit on the number of objects to return, ranging between 1 and 100.
L73: 
L74: - `starting_after` (optional object ID)
L75:   A cursor to use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` to fetch the next page of the list.
L76: - `ending_before` (optional object ID)
L77:   A cursor to use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` to fetch the previous page of the list.
L78: ## List Response Format
L79: 
L80: - `object` (string, value is "list")
L81:   A string that provides a description of the object type that returns.
L82: 
L83: - `data` (array)
L84:   An array containing the actual response elements, paginated by any request parameters.
L85: 
L86: - `has_more` (boolean)
L87:   Whether or not there are more elements available after this set. If `false`, this set comprises the end of the list.
L88: 
L89: - `url` (url)
L90:   The URL for accessing this list.
L91: ## v2 API pagination
L92: 
L93: APIs within the `/v2` namespace contain a different [pagination](https://docs.stripe.com/api-v2-overview.md#list-pagination) interface than the `v1` namespace.
